The image shows soybean leaves with several key symptoms. There are angular, brown lesions on the leaf surfaces. Some of these lesions appear to have caused the tissue to fall out, resulting in a "shot-hole" or ragged appearance. Additionally, there are some larger, irregular brown patches which are likely the result of smaller lesions coalescing. Faint yellow halos can be observed around some of the smaller spots.

Reviewing the provided descriptions, these symptoms strongly align with **Bacterial_Blight**. The description for Bacterial Blight specifically mentions "angular lesions on leaves progressing from yellow-brown to dark reddish-brown centers with yellowish-green halos" and that "infected tissue may fall out giving leaves a ragged appearance." While other diseases like Brown Spot or Septoria Brown Spot cause similar spots, the combination of angularity, color, halos, and the tissue falling out makes Bacterial Blight the best fit.
